invoice-essentials.name: What an invoice must contain
invoice-essentials.title: What a Czech invoice must contain and why
invoice-essentials.lead: Students learn the required details of an invoice under three Czech laws – the VAT Act, the Accounting Act and the Civil Code – and find them on a real document in the demo.
invoice-essentials.metaDescription: Ready-to-teach business school lesson: required invoice details under § 29 of the Czech VAT Act, § 11 of the Accounting Act and § 435 of the Civil Code. Demo task and worksheet with answers.
goals: List the required details of a tax document under § 29(1) of the VAT Act.
Tell what a VAT payer puts on an invoice and what a non-payer does.
Explain why a company invoice must show its entry in the Commercial Register.
Spot a missing or wrong detail on a sample invoice.
teacherNotes: Three laws look at an invoice: the VAT Act (tax document, payers only), the Accounting Act (accounting document) and the Civil Code (business document). Drawing them on the board as three overlapping circles helps.

A non-payer does not issue a tax document. Their invoice still has to meet § 11 of the Accounting Act and § 435 of the Civil Code. The law does not require the words "Not a VAT payer", but they are good practice and save questions.
In the app an invoice gets its number only when it is issued; a draft has none. A good discussion question: why must the number series have no gaps or duplicates?
A simplified tax document (up to CZK 10,000, § 30 and § 30a) is worth a mention. Students know it from receipts.

timeline.text: Hook: show two invoices, one without the customer's VAT number. Who spots the difference and why does it matter?
Explanation: three laws and what they require, payer vs non-payer.
Demo task: take apart a finished invoice and issue a new one.
Worksheet in pairs.
Summary and answer check.

concepts.title: Tax document (VAT payer)
concepts.body: Under § 29(1) of the VAT Act it contains: supplier and customer details, both VAT numbers (DIČ), the document number, the scope and subject of the supply, the issue date, the date of the taxable supply (if it differs from the issue date), the unit price without VAT and any discount, the tax base, the VAT rate and the VAT amount in Czech crowns. It must be issued within 15 days (§ 28(8)).

concepts.title: Accounting document
concepts.body: Under § 11 of the Accounting Act every accounting document has a designation, the content of the transaction and its parties, the amount (or unit price and quantity), when it was made, when the transaction took place (if different) and the signature record of the responsible people.

concepts.title: Business document
concepts.body: Under § 435 of the Civil Code every business shows on its business documents its name and registered office, its company ID (IČO) if it has one, and its entry in a public register including the section and file number. A sole trader who is not in the Commercial Register states their entry in another register, typically the Trade Register.

concepts.title: Simplified tax document
concepts.body: Up to CZK 10,000 in total a payer may issue a simplified document (§ 30). It may leave out the customer's details, the unit price, the tax base and the VAT amount; without the VAT amount it must state the total (§ 30a).

task.intro: You work as an accounting assistant at Lipová stezka s.r.o., a VAT-registered company from Brno. First you check a finished invoice, then you issue a new one.
steps: In the menu open Invoices and click any paid invoice.
On the preview find all twelve details from § 29(1) and tick them off in the worksheet table. For each, note where it is on the document.
Find the Commercial Register entry (file number). Which law requires it?
Click New invoice. Pick a customer marked Verified in ARES and add two lines: Consultation, 2 hours at CZK 1,200, and Licence, 1 piece at CZK 5,000.
Look at the Tax point date field. If you leave it empty, the issue date is used. Why does the law allow that? (Hint: § 29(1)(h).)
Click Save draft and then Issue. Before issuing, the app checks the required details. If it reports anything, write down what and fix it.
Download the PDF and compare it with your table from step 2.
task.check: Done when the student has an issued invoice with a number and every detail from § 29(1) ticked off in the table, with where it appears on the document.

worksheet.q: Name at least eight required details of a tax document.
worksheet.a: Supplier details, supplier VAT number, customer details, customer VAT number, document number, scope and subject of the supply, issue date, date of the taxable supply, unit price without VAT and discount, tax base, VAT rate, VAT amount in CZK (§ 29(1)(a) to (l)).

worksheet.q: A non-payer invoices a bicycle repair. Must the invoice show a VAT rate and amount?
worksheet.a: No. A non-payer does not issue a tax document and does not show VAT. The invoice must meet § 11 of the Accounting Act and § 435 of the Civil Code (name, registered office, IČO, register entry).

worksheet.q: The date of the taxable supply is missing. When is that fine?
worksheet.a: When it is the same as the issue date (§ 29(1)(h)).

worksheet.q: Why must an s.r.o. state the section and file number of the Commercial Register on its invoice?
worksheet.a: An invoice is a business document and § 435 of the Civil Code requires the entry in a public register including the section and file number.

worksheet.q: A payer delivered goods on 3 March. By when must the tax document be issued?
worksheet.a: Within 15 days of the day the obligation to declare the tax arose (§ 28(8)), so by 18 March.

worksheet.q: A customer paid CZK 7,900 in a payer's e-shop and wants a document. Must it show their name?
worksheet.a: No. Up to CZK 10,000 a simplified tax document may be issued (§ 30), which does not need the customer's details (§ 30a).

vat-payers-and-registries.name: VAT payers, non-payers and partner checks
vat-payers-and-registries.title: VAT payer, non-payer and checking a business partner in public registers
vat-payers-and-registries.lead: When a Czech business becomes a VAT payer, how that shows on the invoice, and how to check a customer's IČO and VAT number in ARES, the VAT payer register and VIES in a few minutes.
vat-payers-and-registries.metaDescription: Lesson: Czech VAT registration threshold (§ 6 of the VAT Act), payer vs non-payer invoices, checking IČO in ARES, unreliable payers and published bank accounts, VAT numbers in VIES.
goals: Explain when a taxable person becomes a VAT payer (§ 6 of the VAT Act).
Compare a non-payer's and a payer's invoice and name the differences.
Check an IČO in ARES and a VAT number in VIES and explain what an unreliable payer is.
Explain why it pays to check the supplier's published bank account.
teacherNotes: Since 2025 the threshold is counted per calendar year: a person becomes a payer from 1 January of the year after their turnover exceeded CZK 2,000,000. If turnover exceeds CZK 2,536,500 during the year, they are a payer from the following day (§ 6(1) and (2)). The registration application is due within 10 working days (§ 94(1)).
Have students work out the threshold on paper from a table of monthly sales. The app tracks the limit, but the point of the lesson is understanding the rule.

Liability for tax (§ 109) surprises students: a customer may end up paying the supplier's VAT if they pay to an unpublished account or to an unreliable payer. A good chance to show why partners are checked before paying, not after.
VIES checks VAT numbers for trade within the EU. The Czech VAT payer register shows status in Czechia including published accounts. They are two different tools.

timeline.text: Question for the class: why would anyone register for VAT voluntarily?
Explanation: threshold, compulsory registration, what changes on the invoice.
Threshold calculation on paper (first part of the worksheet).
Demo task: a non-payer invoice and checking partners in registers.
Answer check, summary.

concepts.title: Registration threshold
concepts.body: A taxable person established in Czechia becomes a payer from 1 January of the following year if their turnover for the calendar year exceeded CZK 2,000,000 (§ 6(1)). If turnover in the current year exceeds CZK 2,536,500, they are a payer from the next day (§ 6(2)(b)).

concepts.title: Non-payer vs payer invoice
concepts.body: A non-payer does not show a VAT number as a payer, a rate or a VAT amount, and charges no VAT. A payer issues a tax document with tax base, rate and VAT (§ 29). For a customer who is a payer the difference matters: they cannot deduct VAT from a non-payer's invoice.

concepts.title: ARES and the VAT payer register
concepts.body: ARES is the public register of economic entities: it confirms IČO, name, registered office and register entry. The VAT payer register on the Financial Administration website shows whether an entity is a payer, whether it is an unreliable payer (§ 106a) and which bank accounts it has published.

concepts.title: Customer liability
concepts.body: A customer is liable for the supplier's unpaid VAT, among other cases, when at the time of supply they know the supplier is an unreliable payer, or when they pay to an account the supplier has not published (§ 109).

concepts.title: VIES
concepts.body: The European Commission's system for checking a VAT number in another EU member state. A valid VAT number in VIES is one of the conditions for VAT-free supplies of goods to the EU and for reverse charge on services.

task.intro: You work for Tereza Málková, a self-employed non-payer. The second part of the task you do for a company that is a payer.
steps: Start the demo for Tereza Málková. In Invoices open any issued invoice and download the PDF. Write down which details from § 29(1) are missing and why.
Open Contacts and click New contact. Type the IČO of any well-known Czech company (you will find it on its website) and click Load from ARES. Compare the loaded details with the company's website.
Look up the same entity by hand at ares.gov.cz and in the VAT payer register on the Financial Administration website. Is it a payer? Has it published an account? Is it an unreliable payer?
Go back to /demo and start the demo of a company that is a VAT payer. In Contacts open the German customer Holzwerk Neumann and look at its VAT number status. Check the same number by hand in VIES.
Compare the payer's invoice with the non-payer's invoice from step 1. Fill in the table of differences in the worksheet.
task.check: Done when the student has filled in the table of differences and written down the check result (ARES, VAT payer register, VIES) for one Czech and one foreign company, with the date of the check.

worksheet.q: A sole trader had turnover of CZK 1,950,000 in 2025. By 31 August 2026 their turnover is CZK 2,100,000. From when are they a payer?
worksheet.a: They did not exceed CZK 2,000,000 in 2025, so they are not a payer from 1 January 2026. In 2026 they exceeded CZK 2,000,000 but not CZK 2,536,500, so they become a payer from 1 January 2027 (§ 6(1)). Had they exceeded CZK 2,536,500 during 2026, they would be a payer from the next day.

worksheet.q: By when must someone who exceeded the threshold apply for registration?
worksheet.a: Within 10 working days of exceeding it (§ 94(1)).

worksheet.q: What do you check in ARES and what in the VAT payer register?
worksheet.a: In ARES the entity's identity (IČO, name, registered office, register entry). In the VAT payer register whether it is a payer, whether it is unreliable and which accounts it has published.

worksheet.q: Why not pay to an account the supplier has not published in the VAT payer register?
worksheet.a: Above the statutory limit the customer would be liable for VAT the supplier does not pay (§ 109).

worksheet.q: What is VIES for?
worksheet.a: Checking a VAT number in another EU member state, for example before a VAT-free supply of goods to the EU or before invoicing a service with reverse charge.

worksheet.q: Must a non-payer show their IČO on the invoice?
worksheet.a: Yes, if they have one (§ 435 of the Civil Code).

tax-point-and-due-dates.name: Tax point and due dates
tax-point-and-due-dates.title: Date of taxable supply, issue date and due date
tax-point-and-due-dates.lead: The three dates on every invoice mean three different things. Students learn to set the tax point (DUZP) for goods and services, count the deadline for issuing and set a sensible due date.
tax-point-and-due-dates.metaDescription: Lesson: date of taxable supply under § 21 of the Czech VAT Act, 15-day deadline for the tax document, due dates under § 1963 of the Civil Code. Demo task with weekends and holidays.
goals: Set the date of the taxable supply for goods, services and partial supplies.
Work out the last day on which a tax document must be issued.
Explain the default due date between businesses and the 60-day limit under § 1963 of the Civil Code.
Spot a due date that falls on a weekend or public holiday.
teacherNotes: Students' most common mistake: mixing up the tax point with the issue date. Show an example where a service ended on 28 April and the invoice is issued on 5 May. The VAT belongs to April.

For services, the supply takes place on the day it is provided or on the day the tax document is issued, whichever comes first (§ 21(3)). Students often do not know that an early invoice moves the tax point forward.

The due date is a contract matter, not a tax one. The default rules are in the Civil Code (§ 1963). A due date on a weekend or holiday is in practice moved to the next working day; the app warns about it.
A non-payer does not have to show the tax point, but the Accounting Act wants the moment of the transaction if it differs from the issue date.

timeline.text: Intro: three dates on an invoice, each for a different reader (tax office, accountant, customer).
Explanation: tax point for goods, services and partial supplies, the 15-day deadline, due dates.
Demo task: three invoices with different dates.
Worksheet (date calculations).
Summary.

concepts.title: Tax point for goods
concepts.body: A supply of goods takes place on the day of delivery (§ 21(1) of the VAT Act).

concepts.title: Tax point for services
concepts.body: A service is supplied on the day it is provided or on the day the tax document is issued, whichever is earlier (§ 21(3)). Partial and repeated supplies have special rules (§ 21(7) and (8)).

concepts.title: Deadline for issuing
concepts.body: A tax document must be issued within 15 days of the day the obligation to declare the tax arose (§ 28(8)).

concepts.title: Due date
concepts.body: Between businesses, without an agreement the price is due within 30 days of receiving the invoice or of the supply, whichever is later. A term longer than 60 days applies only if expressly agreed and not grossly unfair to the creditor (§ 1963 of the Civil Code).

task.intro: You invoice for Lipová stezka s.r.o. You create three draft invoices with different dates and see how the app handles them.
steps: Open Invoices and click New invoice. Pick any Czech customer.
Invoice A (goods): add the line Wooden bench, 1 piece, CZK 8,000. The goods were handed over on the 28th of last month. Set the Tax point date to that day and the issue date to today. Save draft.
Check whether today's issue date meets the 15-day deadline. If not, write down how many days late the invoice is.
Invoice B (service): new invoice, line Garden maintenance, 6 hours at CZK 450. The work finishes next week, but you issue the invoice today. Which tax point do you enter and why? Save draft.
Invoice C (due date): on any invoice set the Due date to the next Saturday. The app shows a warning. Click Move to next working day and write down the new date.
For fun, set the due date on a public holiday (for example 28 October) and see what the app says.
task.check: Done when the student has three saved drafts and for each has written down the tax point, issue date and due date with a short reason citing the provision.

worksheet.q: A carpenter delivered a table on 12 May and invoiced on 20 May. What is the tax point and by when did the invoice have to be issued?
worksheet.a: The tax point is 12 May (§ 21(1)). The document must be issued within 15 days, so by 27 May at the latest (§ 28(8)). Issuing on 20 May is fine.

worksheet.q: A designer issues an invoice on 3 June for a logo delivered on 10 June. What is the tax point?
worksheet.a: 3 June. For a service it is the day it is provided or the day the document is issued, whichever comes first (§ 21(3)).

worksheet.q: A contract between two companies sets no due date. The invoice was received on 2 September, the supply took place on 30 August. When is it due?
worksheet.a: Within 30 days of the later of the two, the receipt of the invoice on 2 September, so on 2 October (§ 1963 of the Civil Code).

worksheet.q: Can a large customer negotiate 90-day payment terms?
worksheet.a: Only if it is expressly agreed and not grossly unfair to the supplier (§ 1963 of the Civil Code). Otherwise the longer term is disregarded.

worksheet.q: The due date falls on Sunday 1 November. What do you do?
worksheet.a: Move it to the next working day so the customer can pay on time, or agree on another date. The app warns about weekends.

vat-rates-and-rounding.name: VAT rates and rounding
vat-rates-and-rounding.title: VAT rates, calculating the tax and rounding
vat-rates-and-rounding.lead: How VAT is calculated from the net price and from the gross price, why an invoice with several rates splits into a VAT summary, and why rounding the total to whole crowns is not part of the tax base.
vat-rates-and-rounding.metaDescription: Lesson: Czech VAT rates 21% and 12% (§ 47 of the VAT Act), calculating VAT under § 37, rounding under § 36(5). Demo task with net and gross prices.
goals: Know the current Czech VAT rates and match them to typical examples.
Calculate VAT from the net amount and from the gross amount.
Build a VAT summary by rate.
Explain how rounding the total is treated.
teacherNotes: Since 2024 Czechia has two rates: the standard 21% and the reduced 12% (§ 47). Let students only browse the annexes listing goods and services at the reduced rate; learning them by heart is pointless.
Calculating from the gross amount under § 37(b): VAT = gross − gross / 1.21 (or 1.12). The old coefficients no longer apply; older textbooks may still show them.
The app rounds each line to hellers and the summary adds up the bases per rate. It does not round the total to whole crowns, so do that by hand on paper.
If the total is rounded to whole crowns, the difference is not part of the tax base (§ 36(5)). A frequent question with cash payments.

timeline.text: Puzzle: how much VAT is in a CZK 59 coffee?
Explanation: rates, calculating from net and from gross, the summary.
Demo task: an invoice with two rates, prices including VAT.
Worksheet: calculations and rounding.
Summary.

concepts.title: Rates
concepts.body: The standard rate is 21%, the reduced rate 12% (§ 47 of the VAT Act). Some supplies are exempt (no rate).

concepts.title: From the net amount
concepts.body: VAT = tax base × rate (§ 37(a)). Example: CZK 1,000 × 21% = CZK 210, total CZK 1,210.

concepts.title: From the gross amount
concepts.body: VAT = gross − gross / 1.21 (reduced rate / 1.12) (§ 37(b)). Example: 1,210 − 1,210 / 1.21 = CZK 210.

concepts.title: Rounding
concepts.body: The total payable may be rounded, but the rounding difference is not part of the tax base (§ 36(5)).

task.intro: Lipová stezka s.r.o. runs a course with refreshments. You issue an invoice with two lines and check the calculation.
steps: Open Invoices and click New invoice. Pick any Czech customer.
Add the line Herbal course, 1 piece, CZK 3,500 net, rate 21%.
Add a line of your choice at the reduced rate of 12% (check the annex of the Act for what qualifies), 1 piece, CZK 480 net.
Look at the VAT summary below the lines. Recalculate the base, VAT and total on a calculator and compare.
Turn on I enter prices incl. VAT and change the first line's price to CZK 4,235. What VAT did the app calculate? Check it by calculating from the gross amount.
Save draft. In the worksheet, round the total to whole crowns and write down the difference and where it belongs.
task.check: Done when the student's manual summary matches the app to the heller and they can say why rounding is not part of the tax base.

worksheet.q: Calculate VAT and the total: tax base CZK 2,450, rate 21%.
worksheet.a: VAT CZK 514.50, total CZK 2,964.50.

worksheet.q: The gross price is CZK 1,344 at 12%. What are the base and the VAT?
An invoice has lines of CZK 1,000 (21%) and CZK 500 (12%). Build the summary.
worksheet.a: 21%: base 1,000, VAT 210. 12%: base 500, VAT 60. Total base 1,500, VAT 270, payable CZK 1,770.

worksheet.q: The total is CZK 2,964.50 and the customer pays cash, so you round to CZK 2,965. Does the tax base change?
worksheet.a: No. The CZK 0.50 rounding difference is not part of the tax base (§ 36(5)).

worksheet.q: Why is calculating from the gross amount useful?
worksheet.a: When I only know the final price (for example from a consumer price list), I can work out the VAT and the base without anything else.

advances-and-proforma.name: Advances and proforma invoices
advances-and-proforma.title: Proforma invoice, tax document for a received payment and final settlement
advances-and-proforma.lead: A proforma invoice is not a tax document. Students go through the whole chain: quote, proforma, payment, tax document for the payment and the final invoice with the advance deducted.
advances-and-proforma.metaDescription: Lesson on advances: the proforma as a request for payment, VAT on a received payment (§ 20a of the Czech VAT Act), tax document within 15 days (§ 28), final settlement. Demo and paper task.
goals: Explain the difference between a proforma invoice and a tax document.
Tell when the obligation to declare VAT arises on a received advance.
Build a final invoice with the paid advance deducted.
Turn a quote into a proforma and a proforma into an invoice in the demo.
teacherNotes: A proforma invoice is only a request for payment. The tax obligation arises not when it is issued but when the payment is received (§ 20a(2)), and only if the supply is specific enough: the goods or service, the rate and the place of supply are known (§ 20a(3)).

After receiving the payment a payer must issue a tax document for the received payment within 15 days (§ 28(1)(d) and (8)). Billanta does not issue this document yet, so students put it together on paper. Say so openly; it is a good chance to show that software is not the law.
The final invoice then shows the whole supply and deducts the advance, including the VAT already declared.
A non-payer does not have this issue: the advance is just a payment and the final invoice deducts it.

timeline.text: Story: a customer orders a custom kitchen and pays half up front. When does the carpenter pay the VAT?
Explanation: proforma, received payment, tax document for the payment, final settlement.
Demo task: quote, proforma, invoice.
On paper: tax document for the received payment and the settlement.
Check and summary.

concepts.title: Proforma invoice
concepts.body: A request to pay an advance. It is not a tax document, has no tax point, and issuing it creates no VAT.

concepts.title: VAT on a received payment
concepts.body: When a payer receives a payment before the supply, they must declare VAT on the day the payment is received (§ 20a(2)), provided the supply is specific enough at that moment (§ 20a(3)).

concepts.title: Tax document for a received payment
concepts.body: The payer issues it within 15 days of receiving the payment (§ 28(1)(d) and (8)). It need not show the scope of the supply if it is not yet known (§ 29(3)(c)).

concepts.title: Final settlement
concepts.body: The final invoice shows the whole supply and deducts the advances on which VAT was already declared. Only the difference is paid.

task.intro: Lipová stezka s.r.o. is preparing a CZK 60,500 job (VAT included) for a municipality and wants a 50% advance.
steps: Open Invoices and find a document of type Quote. Open it and look at the buttons at the top.
Click Create proforma. Set the advance to half the total and save. Note that the document type is Proforma invoice.
Find a proforma in the demo that already has an invoice (look in the Invoices list). Open both and compare: what is the same and what differs?
On your new proforma click Create invoice. Look at the Already paid and Left to pay fields.
On paper, put together the tax document for a received advance of CZK 30,250 including VAT (21%): work out the base and VAT from the gross amount. The app does not issue this document yet.
On paper, put together the settlement: the whole supply, the deducted advance and the balance, separately for base, VAT and total.
task.check: Done when the student has the quote – proforma – invoice chain in the demo and a correct tax document for the payment and settlement on paper (advance: base CZK 25,000, VAT CZK 5,250).

worksheet.q: Is a proforma invoice a tax document?
worksheet.a: No. It is a request for payment; issuing it creates no VAT.

worksheet.q: A payer issued a proforma on 1 March, the customer paid on 10 March, the goods are delivered on 2 April. When must VAT on the advance be declared?
worksheet.a: On 10 March, the day the payment was received (§ 20a(2)), provided the supply is specific enough.

worksheet.q: By when must the tax document for the received payment be issued?
worksheet.a: Within 15 days of receiving the payment, so by 25 March (§ 28(8)).

worksheet.q: An advance of CZK 30,250 including 21% VAT. What are the base and the VAT?
The whole job is CZK 50,000 net and the advance from question 4 was paid. What is the balance?
worksheet.a: Total CZK 60,500 with VAT (base 50,000, VAT 10,500). After deducting the advance: base 25,000, VAT 5,250, balance CZK 30,250.

worksheet.q: A customer paid an advance "for something from the catalogue" but has not chosen what. Does VAT arise?
worksheet.a: No, because the supply is not specific enough: neither the goods nor the rate are known (§ 20a(3)).

credit-notes.name: Credit notes and corrections
credit-notes.title: Credit note, corrective tax document and cancellation
credit-notes.lead: The invoice has gone out and the customer returns goods. Students learn when to issue a corrective tax document, what it must contain and why an issued invoice is never deleted.
credit-notes.metaDescription: Lesson: correcting the tax base (§ 42 of the Czech VAT Act), details of a corrective tax document (§ 45), the 15-day deadline, credit note vs cancellation. Demo task.
goals: Recognise situations where the tax base must be corrected.
List the details of a corrective tax document.
Issue a credit note for an existing invoice in the demo.
Explain why an issued invoice must not be deleted or overwritten.
teacherNotes: In practice people say credit note (dobropis); the Act speaks of a corrective tax document (§ 45). Agree on the terms at the start of the lesson.

The correction is a separate taxable supply made on the day the decisive facts occurred (§ 42(3)), and the document must be issued and delivered within 15 days (§ 42(5)). No correction is possible after seven years from the end of the year of the original supply (§ 42(8)).

In the app an issued invoice has three actions: Issue credit note (return or discount), New invoice with the fix (wrong details) and Cancel. Show the difference on the board before students start clicking.
Mind the rate: a correction uses the rate that applied to the original supply (§ 42(7)).

timeline.text: Situation: a customer returned two of ten chairs. Do we delete the invoice and issue a new one?
Explanation: correcting the tax base, required details, deadlines, credit note vs cancellation.
Demo task: a credit note and an invoice with a fix.
Worksheet.
Summary.

concepts.title: When to correct the tax base
concepts.body: A payer corrects the tax base when, after the supply, something happens that changes it: goods returned, a discount, part of a delivery cancelled (§ 42(1)).

concepts.title: Corrective tax document
concepts.body: It contains supplier and customer details including VAT numbers, the number of the original document, its own number, the reason for the correction, the difference in base, the difference in VAT, the difference in total and the date of the decisive facts (§ 45(1)).

concepts.title: Deadlines
concepts.body: The document must be issued and delivered to the customer within 15 days of the decisive facts (§ 42(5)). No correction is possible after seven years from the end of the year of the original supply (§ 42(8)).

concepts.title: Why not delete the invoice
concepts.body: An issued invoice is an accounting record with a serial number. Deleting it would leave a gap in the series and remove the document the customer may already have used to deduct VAT. A mistake is therefore fixed with a new document.

task.intro: Lipová stezka s.r.o. delivered goods and the customer returns part of them. You put it right.
steps: Open Invoices and find the existing credit note in the demo. Open it and find the details from § 45(1). Which do you find, and how does it refer to the original invoice?
Open any issued invoice with two or more lines. Click Issue credit note.
In the credit note keep only the line the customer is returning and change the quantity as your teacher says. The amounts are negative. Save and issue.
On another invoice try New invoice with the fix. How does it differ from a credit note? When would you use it?
Try to find a Delete button on an issued invoice. Why is there none? Write down your answer.
task.check: Done when the student has an issued credit note referring to the original invoice and can explain the difference between a credit note, an invoice with a fix and a cancellation.

worksheet.q: A customer returned 2 of 10 chairs at CZK 1,500 net each (21%). What are the differences in base, VAT and total on the credit note?
worksheet.a: Base −CZK 3,000, VAT −CZK 630, total −CZK 3,630.

worksheet.q: Name at least five details of a corrective tax document.
worksheet.a: Supplier and customer details, their VAT numbers, number of the original document, number of the corrective document, reason for the correction, difference in base, difference in VAT, difference in total, date of the decisive facts (§ 45(1)).

worksheet.q: Goods were returned on 4 April. By when must the corrective document reach the customer?
worksheet.a: Within 15 days of the decisive facts, so by 19 April (§ 42(5)).

worksheet.q: The original invoice used a rate that has since changed. Which rate goes on the credit note?
worksheet.a: The rate that applied on the day of the original supply (§ 42(7)).

worksheet.q: The invoicing clerk found a typo in the customer's name. Is that a correction of the tax base?
worksheet.a: No, the base does not change. A new invoice with the fix or a corrective document is issued according to internal rules; the issued invoice is not deleted.

foreign-customers-reverse-charge.name: Foreign customers and reverse charge
foreign-customers-reverse-charge.title: Foreign customers: services and goods to the EU and OSS basics
foreign-customers-reverse-charge.lead: When a Czech invoice abroad carries no VAT, what to write instead, and why VAT figures are stated in crowns even on a euro invoice. At the end, a short look at OSS for sales to consumers in the EU.
foreign-customers-reverse-charge.metaDescription: Lesson: place of supply of services (§ 9 of the Czech VAT Act), "daň odvede zákazník" (§ 29(2)), supplies of goods to the EU (§ 64), recapitulative statement, OSS basics. Demo task with a EUR invoice.
goals: Set the place of supply for a service to a business in another EU state.
Issue an invoice with reverse charge and the right wording.
Explain why tax figures are stated in crowns even on a foreign-currency invoice.
Describe what the recapitulative statement and OSS are for.
teacherNotes: The main rule for services between businesses: the place of supply is where the customer is established (§ 9(1)). The customer declares the VAT in their own country and the invoice says "daň odvede zákazník" (the customer accounts for the tax, § 29(2)(c)), with no rate or VAT amount (§ 29(3)(e)).

A supply of goods to a payer in another member state is exempt (§ 64) if the conditions are met (customer's VAT number, transport to another state). The document is issued within 15 days of the end of the month (§ 28(9)).

OSS (the one-stop-shop special scheme, § 110a and following) mainly covers distance sales of goods and services to consumers in other EU states. The app does not support OSS, so explaining the idea and working the example on paper is enough.

The exchange rate is set by § 4(8) of the VAT Act: the ČNB foreign-exchange market rate or the ECB reference rate valid on the day the obligation to declare the tax arose. In class it is enough that the app offers the ČNB rate. Leave the details of conversion to the accounting seminar.

timeline.text: Question: a Brno company invoices a Vienna company for web design. Does it charge Czech VAT?
Explanation: place of supply, reverse charge, goods to the EU, non-EU countries, recapitulative statement.
Demo task: an invoice to Germany in EUR.
OSS by example and the worksheet.
Summary.

concepts.title: Place of supply of a service
concepts.body: For a service to a taxable person, the place of supply is where the recipient is established (§ 9(1)). No Czech VAT is charged.

concepts.title: The customer accounts for the tax
concepts.body: When the customer declares the VAT, the document must say "daň odvede zákazník" (§ 29(2)(c)). The rate and VAT amount are left out (§ 29(3)(e)).

concepts.title: Goods to the EU
concepts.body: A supply of goods to a payer from another member state, dispatched to that state, is exempt (§ 64). The invoice refers to the exemption (§ 29(2)(a)). The supply goes into the recapitulative statement (§ 102).

concepts.title: OSS
concepts.body: When a business sells goods at a distance or services to consumers in other EU states, the customer's country's VAT applies. The one-stop-shop scheme (§ 110a and following) lets it declare and pay that VAT in Czechia without registering in each state.

task.intro: Lipová stezka s.r.o. ran a training course for the German company Holzwerk Neumann. It invoices in euros.
steps: Open Contacts and find Holzwerk Neumann. Check its VAT number status (the VIES label) and write it down.
Open Invoices and find an existing reverse-charge invoice in EUR. Find the reverse-charge wording and the amounts in crowns.
Click New invoice, pick Holzwerk Neumann and set Currency to EUR. Note the ČNB rate the app offers.
Add the line Training – timber construction design, 1 day, EUR 1,200. Turn on Reverse charge. What happened to the VAT rate on the line?
Save draft and download the PDF. Find the wording for the customer and the conversion to crowns.

On paper: a Czech company sells goods through its e-shop to a Slovak consumer for EUR 100 net. Assume its sales to consumers in other EU states exceeded EUR 10,000 in the year, so the customer's country's VAT applies. Calculate VAT at the Slovak standard rate of 23% and write down how the company would pay it under OSS.
task.check: Done when the student has a draft EUR invoice with reverse charge, can point to the words "daň odvede zákazník" and has worked the OSS example on paper (EUR 23 VAT, paid through OSS in Czechia).

worksheet.q: A Czech company (payer) invoices an Austrian company for a translation. Where is the place of supply and who declares the VAT?
worksheet.a: In Austria, where the recipient is established (§ 9(1)). The Austrian customer declares the VAT; the invoice says "daň odvede zákazník".

worksheet.q: What is left out of such an invoice?
worksheet.a: The VAT rate and the VAT amount (§ 29(3)(e)).

worksheet.q: A Czech company sells a machine to a company in Poland and transports it there. Which regime applies?
worksheet.a: An exempt supply of goods to another member state (§ 64), if the customer has a valid VAT number and the goods were transported. The invoice refers to the exemption; the supply goes into the recapitulative statement (§ 102).

worksheet.q: By when is the document issued for a supply of goods to the EU made on 10 May?
worksheet.a: Within 15 days of the end of the month, so by 15 June (§ 28(9)).

worksheet.q: On a EUR invoice the VAT is zero because of reverse charge. In which currency would the VAT amount otherwise be stated?
worksheet.a: In Czech crowns (§ 29(1)(l)).

worksheet.q: What is OSS in one sentence?
worksheet.a: A scheme in which a business declares and pays VAT on sales to consumers in other EU states in one return in Czechia instead of registering in each state.

payment-reminders-late-interest.name: Reminders and late-payment interest
payment-reminders-late-interest.title: Reminders, late-payment interest and limitation
payment-reminders-late-interest.lead: The invoice is overdue. Students write a polite reminder, calculate late-payment interest under the Czech government decree and find out how long the debt can be enforced.
payment-reminders-late-interest.metaDescription: Lesson: late-payment interest (§ 1970 of the Czech Civil Code, Government Decree 351/2013 Coll.), minimum recovery costs of CZK 1,200, limitation (§ 629), automatic reminders in the demo.
goals: Spot an overdue invoice and send a reminder.
Calculate statutory late-payment interest between businesses.
Explain the right to minimum costs of recovering a claim.
Know the general limitation period.
teacherNotes: The interest rate is set by Government Decree No. 351/2013 Coll.: the ČNB repo rate valid on the first day of the calendar half-year in which the delay began, plus 8 percentage points (§ 2(1)). Have students look up the current repo rate on the ČNB website themselves.
Between businesses the creditor is also entitled to minimum recovery costs of CZK 1,200 (§ 3 of the decree).

The app can send reminders, automatically too, but does not calculate late interest. Do the interest calculation on paper. Classroom mode sends no emails (Send reminder ends with an error), so students write the reminder text and show it to the teacher.
The general limitation period is three years (§ 629 of the Civil Code). A good question: when does it start? When the right could first be exercised, typically the day after the due date.

timeline.text: Role play: call a customer who has not paid. What do you say?
Explanation: delay, interest, minimum costs, limitation.
Demo task: a reminder and automatic reminder settings.
Interest calculation on paper.
Summary.

concepts.title: Delay
concepts.body: A debtor is in delay when they do not pay properly and on time. The creditor may then claim late-payment interest (§ 1970 of the Civil Code) without warning them first.

concepts.title: Interest rate
concepts.body: The ČNB repo rate valid on the first day of the calendar half-year in which the delay began, plus 8 percentage points (Government Decree 351/2013 Coll., § 2(1)). The rate stays the same for the whole delay in that half-year.

concepts.title: Calculation
concepts.body: Interest = amount owed × annual rate × days of delay / 365. If the contract sets a different rate, the contractual rate applies.

concepts.title: Minimum costs and limitation
concepts.body: Between businesses the creditor is entitled to CZK 1,200 as minimum costs of recovering the claim (§ 3 of the decree). The general limitation period is three years (§ 629 of the Civil Code).

task.intro: Lipová stezka s.r.o. has several overdue invoices. You write a reminder and set up automation.
steps: Open Invoices and filter the overdue ones. Write down how many there are and their total.

Open one and find out how many days it is overdue and how many reminders the customer has had. Write the reminder text on paper and show it to the teacher. Don't press Send reminder: a class company sends no emails.
Open Settings, the Invoices section, and find Reminders. Find out how automatic sending, the days between reminders and their maximum number are set. Choose your own values and write down why.
In the settings find the email template Reminder to a customer and edit it so it includes the invoice number and amount.
On paper, calculate late interest on the chosen invoice: look up the ČNB repo rate on the first day of the half-year, add 8 percentage points and calculate the interest for the actual days of delay.
task.check: Done when the student has written a reminder checked by the teacher, set up automatic reminders with reasons, and correctly calculated late interest with the repo rate and its source stated.

worksheet.q: An invoice for CZK 50,000 was due on 31 March and paid on 30 April (30 days late). For this example, the repo rate on 1 January was 3.5%. What is the late interest?
What else is a business creditor entitled to besides interest?
worksheet.a: Minimum recovery costs of CZK 1,200 (§ 3 of Government Decree 351/2013 Coll.).

worksheet.q: The delay started in August and lasts until November. Which repo rate do you use?
worksheet.a: The rate valid on 1 July, the first day of the half-year in which the delay began (§ 2(1)).

worksheet.q: An invoice was due on 15 June 2026. Roughly by when must the claim be brought to court so it is not time-barred?
worksheet.a: The limitation period is three years (§ 629 of the Civil Code) and runs from when the claim could first be made, the day after the due date. It ends in mid-June 2029 (the general rule; the law also has cases where the period stops running).

worksheet.q: Why set a maximum number of automatic reminders?
worksheet.a: So the customer does not get endless emails; after the last reminder it makes sense to phone, meet or start collection.

flat-tax.name: Czech flat-rate tax
flat-tax.title: Czech flat-rate tax for the self-employed: who may use it and how to watch the limit
flat-tax.lead: The Czech flat-rate regime (paušální daň) replaces the tax return and insurance statements with one monthly payment. Students find out who may join, how the bands work and how to watch the income limit in the app.
flat-tax.metaDescription: Lesson on the Czech flat-rate tax: conditions (§ 2a of the Income Tax Act), bands by amount and type of income, notice of entry by 10 January, payment by the 20th. Demo task.
goals: List the conditions for joining the flat-rate regime.
Place a self-employed person in the right band by amount and type of income.
Know the deadlines for the notice of entry and the monthly payments.
Track income against the band limit in the demo.
teacherNotes: The flat-rate tax exists only in Czechia. Slovakia has no similar regime; for Slovak sole traders we offer a tax and contributions calculator.

The monthly amounts change every year with the minimum and average wage, so this page deliberately does not state them: have students look up the current amounts on the Financial Administration website or in our flat-tax calculator.

Bands (§ 2a(5) of the Income Tax Act): band one up to CZK 1,000,000 of income of any type, or up to CZK 1,500,000 if at least 75% of income falls under the 80% or 60% flat expense rate, or up to CZK 2,000,000 if at least 75% falls under the 80% rate. Band two up to CZK 1,500,000, or up to CZK 2,000,000 with income under the 80% and 60% rates. Band three up to CZK 2,000,000.

Conditions (§ 2a(1)): a self-employed person who is not a VAT payer (exception: identified person), is not insolvent and has no employment income (with exceptions). The notice of entry is due by 10 January (§ 38lc(1)), the payment by the 20th of the month (§ 38lk(5)).

timeline.text: Question: why would a self-employed person want to pay the same amount every month instead of filing a tax return?
Explanation: conditions, bands, deadlines, what the flat-rate tax covers (income tax, social and health insurance).
Demo task: a self-employed person in the flat-rate regime.
Worksheet: placing in a band.
Summary.

concepts.title: What the flat-rate tax covers
concepts.body: One monthly payment that includes income tax, social insurance and health insurance (§ 7a and § 38li of the Income Tax Act). Someone in the regime for the whole year files neither a tax return nor the statements for social and health insurance.

concepts.title: Who may join
concepts.body: A self-employed person who is not a VAT payer (except an identified person), is not insolvent, has no employment income (with exceptions) and stays within the income limit (§ 2a(1)).

concepts.title: Bands
concepts.body: The three bands differ in the monthly amount. Which band applies depends on the income and on which flat expense rate would apply to it (§ 2a(5)).

concepts.title: Deadlines
concepts.body: Notice of entry by 10 January of the year (§ 38lc(1)). The monthly payment is due by the 20th of the calendar month (§ 38lk(5)).

task.intro: You work for Ondřej Kalina, a self-employed person in the flat-rate regime and a VAT non-payer.
steps: On /demo start the flat-rate freelancer demo. In Invoices add up (or read from the overview) how much Ondřej invoiced over the last twelve months.
Open Settings, the Business details section, and find the question Are you in the flat-tax regime? and the type of activity. Write down what is filled in and why it matters for the band.
Open our flat-tax calculator (link below), enter Ondřej's annual income and type of activity. Which band is he in and how much does he pay a month?
Issue a new invoice for CZK 150,000 and recalculate the annual income. Does Ondřej still fit his band? Is he at risk of moving to a higher band or leaving the regime?
Look up the current monthly amounts for all three bands on the Financial Administration website (link below) and write them in the worksheet.
task.check: Done when the student can say which band Ondřej is in, how much he pays a month (per the Financial Administration's current figures) and how much is left before the band limit.

worksheet.q: A graphic designer (non-payer, no employment) had income of CZK 900,000 last year. Can she join the flat-rate regime, and in which band?
worksheet.a: Yes, she meets the conditions (§ 2a(1)). She belongs in band one, as her income did not exceed CZK 1,000,000.

worksheet.q: A tradesman (80% flat expense rate) has income of CZK 1,800,000. Which band?
worksheet.a: Band one, because at least 75% of his income falls under the 80% rate and it did not exceed CZK 2,000,000 (§ 2a(5)).

worksheet.q: A programmer (60% flat expense rate) has income of CZK 1,800,000. Which band?
worksheet.a: Band two: band one for the 60% rate ends at CZK 1,500,000, band two for the 80% and 60% rates goes up to CZK 2,000,000.

worksheet.q: By when is the notice of entry into the flat-rate regime filed?
worksheet.a: By 10 January of the year from which the person wants to be in the regime (§ 38lc(1)).

worksheet.q: By when is the monthly payment due?
worksheet.a: By the 20th of the calendar month (§ 38lk(5)).

worksheet.q: Can a VAT payer join the flat-rate regime?
worksheet.a: No, except an identified person (§ 2a(1)).

what-is-an-invoice.name: What an invoice is
what-is-an-invoice.title: What an invoice is and why businesses issue one
what-is-an-invoice.lead: Students find out what an invoice is for, who issues it and to whom, and spot the key details on a real invoice in the demo.
what-is-an-invoice.metaDescription: Financial literacy lesson for lower secondary school: what an invoice is, supplier and customer, amount, issue date and due date. A task in the no-signup demo and a worksheet with answers.
goals: Explain in their own words what an invoice is.
Tell the supplier from the customer.
Find the invoice number, amount, issue date and due date.
Know why invoices are kept.
teacherNotes: The lesson is for students aged about 13 to 15 and fits financial literacy. It is not about tax or accounting; the aim is that students recognise an invoice when they see one at home or in their first job.

Do not dictate paragraphs to students. For you (Czech law): the details a business puts on its business documents (name, registered office, ID number) are set by § 435 of the Civil Code, and an accounting document by § 11 of the Accounting Act.
The demo is Tereza Málková, a graphic designer who is not a VAT payer. Her invoices are therefore simple: one price with no tax added.
A difference students know: they get a receipt in a shop straight away when they pay. An invoice usually comes when payment happens later, most often by bank transfer.

timeline.text: Question for the class: have you seen an invoice at home? What was it for (electricity, internet, phone)?
Explanation: who sells, who buys, what is on an invoice and why it is not just a note on a scrap of paper.
Demo task: find the details on one invoice.
Worksheet.
Summary: one sentence on what an invoice is.

concepts.title: Invoice
concepts.body: A written document in which the seller tells the buyer: this is what I supplied, this is what it costs, and pay me by this date.

concepts.title: Supplier and customer
concepts.body: The supplier sold the goods or service and issues the invoice. The customer bought it, receives the invoice and pays.

concepts.title: What is on an invoice
concepts.body: The invoice number, who issued it and to whom, what was sold, what it costs, when it was issued and by when it must be paid (the due date). A business also adds its company ID number.

concepts.title: Why keep invoices
concepts.body: An invoice proves that a sale happened and for how much. A business needs it for accounting and tax, a buyer for a complaint, for example.

task.intro: In the demo you are Tereza Málková, a graphic designer. You look at the invoices she has already issued.
steps: Open Invoices. How many invoices do you see in the list?
Open one paid invoice. Write down the invoice number, the supplier, the customer and the total.
Find the issue date and the due date. How many days did the customer have to pay?
Look at the invoice lines. What exactly did Tereza sell?
Find the sentence about VAT on the invoice. What do you think it means?
task.check: Done when the student correctly writes down the invoice number, supplier, customer, amount and both dates and says in their own words what an invoice is for.

worksheet.q: Who issues the invoice: the supplier or the customer?
worksheet.a: The supplier, the one who sold or did something.

worksheet.q: A family received an invoice for internet. Who is the supplier and who is the customer?
worksheet.a: The supplier is the internet provider. The customer is the family member whose name is on the contract.

worksheet.q: An invoice was issued on 1 March and is due on 15 March. How many days are there to pay?
worksheet.a: 14 days.

worksheet.q: What is the difference between a shop receipt and an invoice?
worksheet.a: We get a receipt when we pay on the spot. An invoice arrives and is paid later, usually by bank transfer.

worksheet.q: Why not throw an invoice away as soon as it is paid?
worksheet.a: It proves what was bought and for how much, which helps with a complaint. A business also needs it for accounting and tax.

law.label: Civil Code No. 89/2012 Coll., § 435 – details on business documents (in Czech)
Accounting Act No. 563/1991 Coll., § 11 – accounting document (in Czech)

first-invoice.name: My first invoice
first-invoice.title: My first invoice: a sole trader who is not a VAT payer
first-invoice.lead: Students try issuing an invoice as a new sole trader who is not a VAT payer: they add a customer, fill in the lines and issue the invoice.
first-invoice.metaDescription: Lesson for lower secondary school: a first invoice from a non-VAT-payer step by step – customer, lines, due date, issuing. A task in the no-signup demo and a worksheet with answers. Czech rules.
goals: Create a new customer.
Fill in the invoice lines: what, how many and at what price.
Set the due date.
Issue the invoice and check it.
teacherNotes: A business that is not a VAT payer adds no tax to its price, so its invoice is simpler. Under Czech law a business becomes a payer once its turnover for 12 consecutive months exceeds CZK 2,000,000 (§ 6 of the VAT Act). One sentence is enough for students.

The law does not require the sentence “I am not a VAT payer”, but it is common practice: the customer sees at once that the price contains no tax. The app adds it to a non-payer's invoice automatically.
The trader's name, address and ID number on the invoice are required by § 435 of the Civil Code. The app fills them in from the company settings.
In classroom mode invoices are not sent by email. Issuing the invoice and looking at it on screen is enough.
Make up a job with the class, such as a logo for the school band or a poster for a fair, and let students invoice it.

timeline.text: Story: Tereza drew a logo for a new café. How does she get paid?
Explanation: customer, lines, due date and what happens once the invoice is issued.
Demo task: a new customer and an invoice.
Check in pairs and the worksheet.
Summary.

concepts.title: Not a VAT payer
concepts.body: A sole trader with smaller sales adds no value added tax to the price. The invoice has one price, and that is what the customer pays.

concepts.title: Customer
concepts.body: Who you invoice. For a company, entering its ID number is enough: the app fills in the name and address from the register.

concepts.title: Line
concepts.body: One row of the invoice: what you supplied, how much of it and the unit price. The app adds up the total.

concepts.title: Due date
concepts.body: The day by which the customer should pay. It is often 14 days after the invoice is issued.

concepts.title: Issuing
concepts.body: While the invoice is a draft you can change anything. Once issued it is a finished invoice, and mistakes are no longer fixed by overwriting it but with a new document.

task.intro: You are Tereza Málková. You drew a logo for a new company and arranged business card printing too.
steps: Open Contacts and click New contact. Create the customer: a company by the ID number your teacher writes on the board, or a made-up company with details typed in by hand.
Open Invoices and create a new invoice. Choose your new contact as the customer.
Add a line “Logo design”: quantity 1, price CZK 6,000. Add a second line “Business card printing”: 200 pieces at CZK 3.
Check that the total is CZK 6,600 and that the due date is 14 days from today.
Issue the invoice. In the preview find your ID number, the customer, the invoice number and the sentence about VAT.
task.check: Done when the student has issued an invoice for CZK 6,600 to a new customer with the right due date and can point to the invoice number, the ID number and the amount on it.

worksheet.q: Tereza is not a VAT payer. The logo costs CZK 6,000. How much does the customer pay?
worksheet.a: CZK 6,000. A non-payer adds nothing to the price.

worksheet.q: Line: 200 business cards at CZK 3. What is the total?
worksheet.a: CZK 600.

worksheet.q: An invoice is issued on 10 May and due in 14 days. By when should it be paid?
worksheet.a: By 24 May.

worksheet.q: Why do you enter a company's ID number?
worksheet.a: The ID number identifies the company in the register without doubt, even if another company has the same name.

worksheet.q: A classmate forgot to write what they sold on the invoice. Why is that a problem?
worksheet.a: The customer does not know what they are paying for, and the invoice does not prove what was supplied.

paid-or-unpaid.name: Paid or not?
paid-or-unpaid.title: Paid or not? The due date in practice
paid-or-unpaid.lead: Students learn to tell which invoices are paid, which are still waiting and which are overdue, and mark one invoice as paid themselves.
paid-or-unpaid.metaDescription: Lesson for lower secondary school: the due date, paid, unpaid and partly paid invoices, overdue invoices. A task in the no-signup demo and a worksheet on counting days. Czech rules.
goals: Explain what a due date is.
Tell a paid, an unpaid and an overdue invoice apart.
Work out how many days an invoice is overdue.
Record a received payment in the app.
teacherNotes: One rule for students: an invoice not paid by its due date is overdue, and the customer is in delay. The supplier can then claim late-payment interest (§ 1970 of the Czech Civil Code); the reminder lesson covers the details.

The parties agree the due date. Between businesses Czech law allows more than 60 days only if it is not grossly unfair to the creditor (§ 1963 of the Civil Code). For students it is enough that the due date should always be on the invoice.
The demo has paid, unpaid and overdue invoices, and one that is only partly paid. Students tell them apart by the status in the list.
In real life an invoice is marked as paid only once the money has actually arrived. In class you play it out: the teacher announces which payment has “just come in”.

timeline.text: Question: you lent a friend CZK 100 and they promised to pay it back by Friday. It is Monday and nothing. What now?
Explanation: the due date, invoice statuses, overdue, partial payment.
Demo task: the invoice list, a filter, marking a payment.
Worksheet: counting days.
Summary.

concepts.title: Due date
concepts.body: The last day by which the customer should pay. It is written on the invoice.

concepts.title: Paid invoice
concepts.body: The full amount has arrived. The invoice is settled.

concepts.title: Unpaid invoice
concepts.body: The money has not arrived yet, but the due date has not passed. Nothing is wrong; you wait.

concepts.title: Overdue
concepts.body: The due date has passed and the money has not arrived, or only part of it has. The rest is still a debt and the supplier should get in touch.

task.intro: You are Tereza Málková and want to know who still owes you money.
steps: Open Invoices. Find the status of each invoice. How many are paid and how many unpaid?
In the filter choose Overdue. Which invoices are they and how much do they add up to?
Find the invoice that is only partly paid. How much is still left to pay?
The teacher announces that one unpaid invoice has just been paid into the account. Open it and click Mark as paid, Paid today.
Go back to the list. How did the invoice status change, and how much do customers owe you in total now?
task.check: Done when the student lists the overdue invoices and their total, finds the partly paid invoice and marks one invoice as paid.

worksheet.q: An invoice is due on 20 April. Today is 18 April and no money has come. Is it overdue?
worksheet.a: No. The due date has not passed yet; the invoice is unpaid but fine.

worksheet.q: An invoice was due on 10 June and today is 25 June. How many days overdue is it?
worksheet.a: 15 days.

worksheet.q: An invoice is for CZK 4,000 and the customer sent CZK 3,000. Is it paid?
worksheet.a: Only partly. CZK 1,000 is still to be paid.

worksheet.q: Why is an invoice marked as paid only when the money arrives, not when the customer promises to pay?
worksheet.a: A promise is not a payment. Until the money is in the account, the debt remains.

worksheet.q: An invoice is issued on 1 September and due in 30 days. By when should it be paid?
worksheet.a: By 1 October (September has 30 days).

simple-reminder.name: A simple reminder
simple-reminder.title: A simple reminder: asking politely for your money
simple-reminder.lead: A customer has not paid. Students write a short, polite reminder with nothing important missing and compare it with the template in the app.
simple-reminder.metaDescription: Lesson for lower secondary school: what a payment reminder is, what it must include and what tone it should take. A task in the no-signup demo, writing a reminder and a worksheet with answers. Czech rules.
goals: Explain what a reminder is for.
Write a polite reminder with all the important details.
Tell a polite tone from an unsuitable one.
Know what can follow when the debtor still does not pay.
teacherNotes: A reminder is not compulsory and the law does not say what it should look like. It is a polite nudge; often the customer simply forgot or made a mistake with the payment.

Between businesses the supplier can claim late-payment interest (§ 1970 of the Czech Civil Code) and at least CZK 1,200 as costs of recovering the debt (Government Decree No. 351/2013 Coll.). Students only need to know that paying late can get expensive. The interest calculation is in the secondary-school lesson.
Students write the reminder on paper. They do not send it from the demo; classroom mode sends no emails.
A good reminder has six things: who is writing, the invoice number, the amount owed, the original due date, how to pay and a new deadline. No threats.

timeline.text: Two sample reminders on the projector: one polite, one aggressive. Which would make you pay?
Explanation: what a reminder contains and what tone it should take.
In the demo: find an overdue invoice and read the reminder template.
Students write their own reminder and correct it in pairs.
Summary: what to do when even a reminder does not help.

concepts.title: Reminder
concepts.body: A short message telling the customer that an invoice is overdue and has not been paid yet.

concepts.title: What it must include
concepts.body: The invoice number, the amount owed, the original due date, the account number or another way to pay, and a new date to pay by.

concepts.title: Tone
concepts.body: Polite and to the point. The customer may have forgotten or sent the payment wrongly. Threats and insults spoil the relationship and do not bring the money in.

concepts.title: If it does not help
concepts.body: Next comes a phone call, a second reminder, perhaps an agreement to pay in instalments, and in the end debt collection. The supplier can also ask for interest for the late payment.

task.intro: You are Tereza Málková. One of your invoices is overdue and you want to remind the customer to pay.
steps: Open Invoices and filter Overdue. Pick one invoice and write down its number, the customer, the amount and the due date.
Work out how many days overdue the invoice is.
Open Settings, the Emails section, and read the reminder template. Which details does the app fill in by itself?
Write your own reminder on paper: greeting, invoice number, amount, original due date, account number, a new deadline (for example in 7 days) and your name.
Swap reminders with your neighbour. Is anything missing? Is it polite?
task.check: Done when the student has written a polite reminder with all six details and can say what they will do if the customer still does not pay.

worksheet.q: What does it mean that an invoice is overdue?
worksheet.a: The due date has passed and the invoice is still not paid.

worksheet.q: Which details must a reminder include so the customer knows what to pay and how?
worksheet.a: The invoice number, the amount, the original due date, payment details and a new deadline.

worksheet.q: Is “Pay now or else!” a suitable sentence? Why?
worksheet.a: No. It is threatening, harms the relationship with the customer and explains nothing.

worksheet.q: The reminder did not work. What can the supplier do next?
worksheet.a: Call, send a second reminder, agree on instalments and finally pursue the debt.

worksheet.q: Does the supplier get anything extra for a late payment?
worksheet.a: Between businesses they can claim late-payment interest and at least CZK 1,200 as recovery costs.

vat-return-control-statement.name: VAT return and control statement
vat-return-control-statement.title: VAT return and control statement: from documents to the form
vat-return-control-statement.lead: From one month of issued and received invoices, students build a VAT return on paper, sort the documents into the sections of the control statement and work out the fines for filing late.
vat-return-control-statement.metaDescription: Lesson for colleges, universities and courses: tax periods, deadlines, the VAT liability, control statement sections and fines under § 101h of the Czech VAT Act. A demo task and a worksheet with answers.
goals: Determine a payer's tax period and the deadline for the return and the control statement.
Calculate output VAT, input VAT deduction and the resulting liability.
Put a document into the right section of the control statement.
Explain when a control statement fine applies and how high it is.
teacherNotes: The tax period is a calendar month (§ 99 of the Czech VAT Act). A payer with turnover up to CZK 15,000,000 that is not an unreliable payer or a group member may choose quarters if it notifies by the end of January, but not in the year of registration or the year after (§ 99a).

The return is due within 25 days after the tax period ends (§ 136(4) of the Tax Procedure Code) and must be filed electronically (§ 101a of the VAT Act). A legal entity files the control statement monthly within 25 days of the month end, a natural person within the return deadline (§ 101e). The deadline cannot be extended.

Fines under § 101h(1): CZK 1,000 for filing late without a notice, CZK 10,000 for filing only in the substitute deadline after a notice, CZK 30,000 for not amending, completing or confirming it when asked, and CZK 50,000 for not filing at all. Fines b) to d) are halved for natural persons and quarterly payers, among others (para. 2). The first late filing under a) in a calendar year is not fined (§ 101j).

The CZK 10,000 incl. VAT threshold splitting sections A.4/A.5 and B.2/B.3 comes from the form instructions, not directly from the Act. Return lines: output VAT at 21 % and 12 % on lines 1 and 2, deduction on lines 40 and 41.

The demo is Lipová stezka s.r.o., a monthly payer. The return and control statement export is an XML file for the Czech tax portal; classroom mode does not download it, so students calculate on paper. The teacher can show the export in the public demo.
In classroom mode, create a class with the Standard or Advanced level for this lesson. The Basics level switches off Expenses, Bank and Reports.

timeline.text: Explanation: tax periods, deadlines, electronic filing.
The structure of the return and the control statement on the projector.
Demo task: last month's documents, recording a received invoice, calculating and sorting into sections.
Worksheet: calculation and fines.
Summary: what happens if the control statement is not filed.

concepts.title: Tax period
concepts.body: A month, or a quarter under the conditions of § 99a. For each period the payer files a return and pays the tax within 25 days of its end.

concepts.title: Output VAT and deduction
concepts.body: The payer pays over the VAT on issued invoices and deducts the VAT on received ones. The difference is the liability; a negative difference is an excess deduction refunded to the payer.

concepts.title: Control statement
concepts.body: A list of the individual documents behind the return. The tax administration uses it to pair suppliers with customers and find documents that one side reported and the other did not.

concepts.title: Sections
concepts.body: A.4 issued documents over CZK 10,000 incl. VAT, A.5 other issued documents in total; B.2 received over CZK 10,000, B.3 other received in total; A.1 and B.1 supplies under the reverse charge.

concepts.title: Right to deduct
concepts.body: It arises only with a tax document (§ 73(1)). It can be claimed at the latest in the return for a period ending by the end of the second calendar year after the year it arose.

task.intro: You are the accountant of Lipová stezka s.r.o. preparing the data for last month's return.
steps: Open Invoices and filter issued invoices with a tax point in the previous month. List the tax base and VAT by rate.

Open Expenses, click New expense and record a received invoice: supplier Kancelář Plus s.r.o., description Meeting room rental, amount incl. VAT CZK 14,520, VAT rate 21 %, tax date in the previous month, document number FV-2026-118.
List the VAT on all received documents with a tax point in the previous month. Mark the reverse-charge document from Montáže Kraus separately.
On paper, calculate output VAT, the deduction and the resulting liability.
Put each document into a control statement section (A.4, A.5, B.2, B.3 or B.1) and explain why.
Write down the date by which the company must file the return and the control statement and pay the tax.
task.check: Done when the student has recorded the new expense, calculated the month's liability correctly and put each document into the right control statement section with a reason.

worksheet.q: For August 2026 a payer has issued invoices with a tax base of CZK 100,000 at 21 % and CZK 20,000 at 12 %, and received invoices with a base of CZK 50,000 at 21 %. What is the liability?
worksheet.a: Output 21,000 + 2,400 = CZK 23,400, deduction CZK 10,500, payable CZK 12,900.

worksheet.q: By when must an s.r.o. file the return and the control statement for August 2026?
worksheet.a: By 25 September 2026, both electronically.

worksheet.q: Which section does a received invoice for CZK 14,520 incl. VAT from a domestic payer go into?
worksheet.a: B.2, because it is over CZK 10,000 incl. VAT. It is listed individually with the supplier's VAT number and the document number.

worksheet.q: An s.r.o. filed its control statement three days late, for the first time this year and without a notice. What fine does it face?
worksheet.a: None. The CZK 1,000 fine under § 101h(1)(a) is not imposed for the first such delay in a calendar year (§ 101j).

worksheet.q: A company registered for VAT in March 2026. Can it file quarterly from January 2027?
worksheet.a: No. Quarters cannot be chosen in the year of registration or the following year, so 2028 at the earliest.

worksheet.q: An invoice with a 2026 tax point arrived late. What is the latest the deduction can be claimed?
worksheet.a: In the return for a period ending no later than 31 December 2028.

bank-matching-expenses.name: Bank matching and expenses
bank-matching-expenses.title: Matching bank payments and recording expenses
bank-matching-expenses.lead: Students go through a company's bank transactions, match payments to invoices, decide what to do with a short payment, a payment without a variable symbol and a bank fee, and record a received document as an expense.
bank-matching-expenses.metaDescription: Lesson for colleges, universities and courses: matching payments by variable symbol, short payments, payments without a reference, bank fees and recording received documents. A demo task and a worksheet with answers. Czech rules.
goals: Match an incoming payment to an invoice and explain what the match is based on.
Decide what to do with a short payment, a payment without a variable symbol and a bank fee.
Record a received document as an expense with the right base and VAT.
Explain why and for how long documents are archived.
teacherNotes: The demo bank transactions are prepared: one payment covered only 90 % of the invoice, an advance of CZK 2,500 from Petr Novotný came without a variable symbol, and a bank fee of −CZK 199 is already ignored. Each one leads to a different question.
Ignoring the fee in matching does not remove it from the books. The accountant books it from the bank statement as a cost; it just is not matched to an invoice.

Deducting VAT on a received document requires a tax document (§ 73(1)(a) of the Czech VAT Act). A payer keeps tax documents for 10 years from the end of the tax period in which the supply took place (§ 35(2)). Accounting records are archived for at least 5 years, the financial statements for 10 (§ 31 of the Accounting Act).
Classroom mode has no real bank connection. Students work with sample transactions and match them by hand.
In classroom mode, create a class with the Standard or Advanced level for this lesson. The Basics level switches off Expenses, Bank and Reports.

timeline.text: Explanation: the statement, the variable symbol, what matching means.
Demo task: go through Bank and resolve each unmatched transaction.
Recording a received document as an expense and checking the report.
Worksheet.
Summary.

concepts.title: Matching
concepts.body: Assigning a bank transaction to an invoice. The app suggests matches by variable symbol and amount; once matched, the invoice becomes paid or partly paid.

concepts.title: Short payment
concepts.body: Less arrived than the invoice amount. The invoice stays partly paid and the rest is chased, unless it is an agreed discount, which then needs a proper document.

concepts.title: Payment without a variable symbol
concepts.body: Without the variable symbol (the Czech payment reference) a payment cannot be matched automatically. You look it up by payer name and amount, or ask the payer.

concepts.title: Expense and received document
concepts.body: Every purchase is recorded with its document: supplier, date, amount, VAT rate and document number. A VAT payer claims the VAT deduction from it.

task.intro: You are the accountant of Lipová stezka s.r.o., checking the bank and documents at month end.
steps: Open Bank. How many transactions are to match? Go through them one by one.
Match each transaction whose variable symbol and amount fit an invoice: click Match and choose the invoice.
Find the payment that covered only 90 %. Match it and look at the invoice status now. How much is left to pay?
Find the CZK 2,500 payment from Petr Novotný without a variable symbol. Which invoice or advance do you think it belongs to? Write down how you would check.
Find the ignored −CZK 199 fee. Why is it not matched to an invoice, and where does it show up in the books?

Open Expenses, click New expense and record a document: supplier Papírnictví Pod Lipou, description Office supplies, amount incl. VAT CZK 6,050, VAT rate 21 %, date today, document number 2026-0412. What are the base and the VAT?
Find this month's costs in Reports and check that the new expense is included. Which expense is still unpaid?
task.check: Done when the student has matched the payments, can say what to do with the short payment, the payment without a variable symbol and the fee and why, and has recorded an expense with a base of CZK 5,000 and VAT of CZK 1,050.

worksheet.q: An invoice is for CZK 12,100 and CZK 10,890 arrived. How much is outstanding and what status does the invoice keep?
worksheet.a: CZK 1,210. The invoice stays partly paid until the rest arrives.

worksheet.q: What is a payment most often matched to an invoice by?
worksheet.a: The variable symbol, which is usually the invoice number, and the amount.

worksheet.q: A document is for CZK 6,050 incl. 21 % VAT. What are the base and the VAT?
worksheet.a: Base CZK 5,000, VAT CZK 1,050.

worksheet.q: A payment arrived without a variable symbol. What do you do?
worksheet.a: Assign it to an invoice or advance by payer name, amount and date; if that is not clear-cut, ask the payer. Do not guess.

worksheet.q: How long must a VAT payer keep tax documents?
worksheet.a: 10 years from the end of the tax period in which the supply took place (§ 35 of the VAT Act).
